outcome: Maternal morbidity (composite including: death, sepsis, ICU admission, acute kidney injury, postpartum dilation and curettage, postpartum hysterectomy, venous thromboembolism, postpartum hemorrhage, postpartum wound complication, postpartum endometritis, pelvic abscess, postpartum pneumonia, readmission, and/or need for blood transfusion)
Severe maternal morbidity (composite including: death, ICU admission, venous thromboembolism, acute kidney injury, postpartum hysterectomy, sepsis, and/or transfusion >2 units)
cohort: 361 patients with preterm prelabor rupture of membranes at ≥23 weeks gestational age
finding: Cesarean delivery, BMI ≥40 at admission, private insurance, and tobacco use were associated with increased odds of maternal morbidity in patients with preterm prelabor rupture of membranes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with increased odds of maternal morbidity in patients with preterm prelabor rupture of membranes.
